title: A Horizon for the Wreck
premise: Sable Villalobos, a nonbinary riverboat captain who has spent fifteen years dodging debts, warrants, and attachments along the Verrazano Reach, discovers a tide-drained cave holding the wreck of the Condesa del Mar—and proof that the salvage concession sold to the powerful Aldous Marchetti family was built on forged papers. When Sable's old crewmate Juno is arrested for a theft she didn't commit, Sable realizes the only evidence that can free her lies sealed inside the wreck, and the concession expires when the first snows close the mountain pass to the land registry. Racing a rival salvager, a corrupt magistrate, and the weather itself, Sable must choose between staying invisible and claiming a name, a crew, and a home. The book ends with Sable testifying at Juno's hearing, surrendering the salvage rights in exchange for her freedom, and piloting the riverboat north with a chosen family aboard as the snows finally fall.
about_author: Beatrix Voss is a former tugboat deckhand who spent six seasons on inland waterways before turning to writing full-time from a houseboat moored outside Astoria. Her fiction draws on river lore, salvage law, and the quiet radicalism of people who live at the water's edge.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine run down the Verrazano Reach establishes Sable's solitary life: measuring days in miles, paying off silent debts, refusing port gossip. When a charter passenger mentions an unusually low tide forecast, Sable dismisses it—but pockets the tide table anyway. Emotional beat: loneliness worn like a comfortable coat.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The freak low tide exposes the mouth of Gullwrack Cave and, inside it, the ribcage of a sunken ship—the legendary Condesa del Mar, lost forty years ago with its manifest sealed. Sable finds a brass strongbox stamped with the Marchetti seal and takes it without deciding to. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Miles
chapters.summary: Juno's POV, via letter and flashback. Juno Reyes, now a dockside clerk in Harrowgate, writes asking Sable for help—she's seen Marchetti surveyors charting the cave approach. The chapter braids their shared history: the mutiny they both fled, the promise Sable broke. Emotional beat: the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Strongbox Problem
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Forced open, the strongbox holds the original Condesa manifest and a bill of sale proving the Marchetti concession rests on a forgery. Sable plans to throw it overboard; instead they hide it under the engine plates. Emotional beat: the moment self-preservation stops being simple.

chapters.title: A Man Named Corliss
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Introduces the antagonist: Dane Corliss, salvage broker working for the Marchettis, charming and ruthless, who boards Sable's boat under pretext of hiring a pilot. He mentions the cave casually, watching Sable's face. Emotional beat: a duel fought entirely in pleasantries.

chapters.title: Harrowgate, After Dark
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable runs upriver to warn Juno and arrives to find her already arrested for stealing Marchetti survey equipment she never touched—a frame job to silence anyone near the cave. Emotional beat: guilt arriving ahead of understanding.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Magistrate Oyelaran's POV. A portrait of institutional rot: Oyelaran knows the charges are thin but owes the Marchettis his seat. He sets Juno's trial for the week after the pass closes—after the concession expires, after any evidence becomes legally worthless. Emotional beat: justice as bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Crew of One No More
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable can't free Juno alone. They reluctantly recruit three outsiders: Tamsin, a disgraced archivist who can authenticate documents; Bo, a teenage stowaway with climbing skills; and Old Ferro, a mechanic who once served on the Condesa. Emotional beat: the terrifying arithmetic of trusting people.

chapters.title: Charts and Confessions
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the boat's cramped cabin, Tamsin authenticates the manifest and uncovers the deeper secret: the Condesa carried not treasure but testimony—depositions against the Marchettis' founding fraud. Ferro admits he was a crewman who survived by keeping silent. Emotional beat: shared shame becoming shared purpose.

chapters.title: Corliss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corliss corners Sable at a lock station: sell the strongbox, walk away rich, and Juno's sentence will be 'managed.' Sable refuses, but realizes Corliss now knows exactly what they carry. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Sabotage at the Weir
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Someone scuttles the riverboat at the night weir; Bo dives into freezing water to save the engine and nearly drowns, saved by Sable. The boat survives, barely, but the schedule is broken—the snows are early this year. Emotional beat: fear of losing everything on one breath.

chapters.title: The River Turns Against Us
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Running the damaged boat through falling temperatures, Ferro reflects on the fifteen years since he abandoned the Condesa's survivors to protect himself. He teaches Sable the old channel markers only Condesa crew knew—markers that lead through the range faster than any map. Emotional beat: an old man buying back a piece of his soul.

chapters.title: Portage of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The river freezes upstream; the crew must portage the boat's essential gear over the shoulder of the Kestrel Range on foot, ahead of the storm. Corliss's hired men shadow them. First blood: a skirmish at a waystation where Bo is injured. Emotional beat: the journey stops being a plan and becomes a siege.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Lost above the treeline in whiteout, the crew shelters in a shepherd's hut. Tamsin confesses why she was disgraced—she once buried evidence for money—and Sable, for the first time, tells someone about the mutiny and the promise to Juno. Emotional beat: confession as survival gear.

chapters.title: The Pass Before the Snows
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A brief clear window lets them cross the summit ridge, but Corliss's men ambush them at the descent. Ferro stays behind to hold the switchback and is captured. Sable must choose: rescue him or make the registry deadline. They choose the deadline, hating themselves. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: Registry of Ashes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the land registry in Coldharbour, Tamsin files the manifest minutes before the concession lapses—but Oyelaran's clerk refuses to enter it, citing procedural irregularities. Legal victory snatched away. Emotional beat: fury at a system designed to outlast outrage.

chapters.title: What Ferro Carried
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Interrogated by Corliss, Ferro reveals he copied the depositions years ago and mailed them to a journalist before his capture. Corliss realizes the secret is already loose—and that his employers will burn him as a loose end. Emotional beat: a coward's last act of courage.

chapters.title: The Trial of Juno Reyes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Back in Harrowgate, Juno's trial begins without the evidence. Sable makes the decision the whole book has bent toward: testify openly, reveal their own fugitive past, and put the mutiny, the cave, and the forgery on the record. Emotional beat: choosing visibility over safety.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Sable's testimony, corroborated by the journalist's published depositions and a shaken Oyelaran flipping on the Marchettis to save himself, collapses the case. Juno walks free; Corliss is arrested fleeing the courthouse. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Marchettis offer Sable full salvage rights and wealth to settle quietly. Sable declines everything except one term: amnesty for Ferro, Bo, and Tamsin, and a registered claim making the cave a public memorial to the Condesa's dead. Emotional beat: power used once, deliberately, then set down.

chapters.title: First Snow on the Reach
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Juno joins the rebuilt riverboat as first mate. The crew casts off from Harrowgate as the season's first snow falls on the water, the strongbox donated to the archive, the past signed and closed. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude in the same breath.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Wreck
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. On the open reach, Sable finally measures life in something other than miles—in people aboard, in mornings shared. The wreck's story belongs to everyone now; Sable's story, at last, belongs to Sable. Final image: the river widening toward the sea, the horizon no longer something to flee. Emotional beat: arrival without an ending.
